overview: White offers the e4 pawn and develops the bishop at once with 3.Bc4 instead of the usual 3.Nc3. Black can take with a developing move such as 3...Nf6 and, after 4.Nc3 or 4.f3, play ...e6, ...c6 or ...Bg4 to consolidate. White hopes for open lines and quick attacks against f7 and h7; strong players regard the compensation as insufficient. I am not certain of the exact branches.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Nc3, Nge2 and Bf4 and use the open f-file or Bc4 to pressure f7.
Break with f3 to open lines, hoping Black's king stays in the centre.

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with ...Nf6 and ...e6 or ...c6 and trade pieces to head for a better endgame.
Hit the bishop with ...Nf6 and ...e6 and develop without weakening.

typical_structures.structure: White d4 pawn with open e-file and f-file; Black with an extra pawn and solid ...c6/...e6 set-up.

character.notes: Open tactical play with White chasing attack for a pawn; sharp for both.

gambit.notes: Black is a pawn up and can keep it with accurate development.

soundness.notes: The BDG is judged insufficient by engines, and this version has even less development support.

structure.notes: Open lines for the pieces from the start.

approach.notes: Rare at strong level; the BDG is a surprise weapon.

level.notes: Dubious so never Beginner; the attacking ideas are easy to follow.

sublines_that_differ.name: Main BDG
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3
sublines_that_differ.how: The standard Blackmar-Diemer, with Nc3 and f3 before the bishop move.

character.reason: Open attacking play for a pawn with a risky king-side attack.

gambit.reason: White gives the e4 pawn and Black can keep it.

structure.reason: Open lines for the pieces from the start.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the BDG.

level.reason: Dubious lines are never Beginner and the attack is easy to follow.

plans.reason: White gives a pawn for speed and an attack.
